title: A Methodology for Assessing the Content-Related Aspect of Intrinsic Motivation in Learning Activity
abstract: The productivity of learning activity in recent research is often linked to the presence of intrinsic motivation, which determines the relevance of this study. The research problem lies in the heterogeneity of intrinsic motivation as the relationship between formal-dynamic and substantive components within Self-Determination Theory and Activity Theory. According to E. Deci and R. Ryan, intrinsic motivation is largely determined by formal-dynamic factors - interest and enjoyment of the activity. A. N. Leontiev not only emphasizes the content of the meaning-making motive but also underscores the change in content (subject matter) as a mechanism for the development of intrinsic motivation. This logic is detailed specifically in the motivation for learning activity. The aim of this study is a pilot approbation of a methodology that distinguishes the content-related side from the formal-dynamic side of intrinsic motivation in student learning activity. Methods. The study involved 93 students from psychology departments in Moscow (ages M = 21.50; SD = 6.99; 80 females). The following instruments were used: the Academic Motivation Questionnaire (Gordeeva, Sychev, Osin, 2014) to assess formal-dynamic intrinsic motivation, and a modified methodology for the involuntary memorization of professional-thematic texts (Dusavitsky, 2012) to assess content-related intrinsic motivation. The texts were structured into four parts: "fact", "theory", "experiment", "application". Results. A significant positive correlation was found between the completeness of recall of the theoretical part of the text and the assessment of interest (r = 0.23, p < 0.05), which confirms the hypothesis about the relationship between content-related intrinsic motivation and interest in theoretical content. When comparing groups of students oriented toward theoretical versus practical content, it was revealed that "theorists" show a tendency toward greater interest in the texts (U = 54, p = 0.073), while "practitioners" show significantly higher positivity of emotions (U = 46, p = 0.036). A positive correlation was found between the completeness of recall of the "experiment" part and the self-development scale of the Academic Motivation Questionnaire (r = 0.22, p < 0.05). Conclusions. The modified involuntary memorization methodology, on the one hand, allows for the empirical separation of the content-related and formal-dynamic sides of intrinsic motivation in student learning activity. On the other hand, a deeper analysis of the formal-dynamic features of intrinsic motivation developed within Self-Determination Theory appears necessary.
